summary.title: Foundational distributed systems papers
summary.one_liner: A categorized, chronologically ordered reading list of foundational distributed systems papers covering clocks, impossibility results, consensus, distributed algorithms, and cloud-scale systems.
keywords: where to start learning distributed systems
takeaways: The list is organized by subject (time and state, impossibility results, consensus, distributed algorithms, miscellaneous, cloud/big data), with papers in chronological order within each section.
Core starting points include Lamport's logical clocks paper, FLP impossibility, Paxos, Viewstamped Replication, and Raft (In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm).
Each section ends with expository papers and blog posts that explain the foundational work more accessibly.
Explicitly excluded topics: networking, security, distributed ledgers, verification work, and distributed transactions (the author plans to cover transactions later).
summary.summary: This is a blog post by Murat Demirbas compiling foundational papers in distributed systems, arranged by subject and chronologically within each section. Topics include time and state (Lamport clocks, distributed snapshots), impossibility results (FLP, CAP, failure detectors), consensus and state machine replication (Paxos, Viewstamped Replication, PBFT, ZooKeeper), distributed algorithms, miscellaneous system design papers, and cloud/big data systems (MapReduce, Dynamo, Spanner). Each section also lists expository papers and blog posts. The page is a bibliography with titles, authors and venues, and it does not explain the papers itself.
